speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what are the considerations behind the Ministry's punitive actions against the employer for the illegal deployment of Ms Parti Liyani as a foreign domestic worker; and (b) whether the actions taken are consistent with similar cases in the past.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Ms Parti Liyani's case of illegal deployment was handled by MOM in accordance with these considerations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The actions taken against the three individuals were in line with actions taken by the Ministry against similar cases in the past.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: About 60 of them were issued with an Advisory Notice; 80 were issued with a Caution.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM will give an update when the review is completed in due course.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Usually, an employment agreement ties an employer with an employee legally.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: So, in this case, I understand that for Ms Parti Liyani, warning letters were issued to Mrs Liew as well as to Mr Karl Liew who were not her employers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: So, in this case, may I ask if the MOM will be reviewing this and to see if the MOM would also be responding to why the letters were actually written to Mrs Liew as well as Mr Karl Liew?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: This is to remind the employers that they are ultimately accountable for their foreign domestic workers and should take steps to ensure that their households' deployment of the foreign domestic workers do not contravene the law.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that the foreign domestic workers or FDWs can be deployed outside their registered address if they are looking after the young children and the senior parents or the elderly parents of the employers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask whether moving forward, MOM can require a documented consent from the FDW if they are going to be deployed outside the registered address?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That way, I think it can sort of resolve some of the disputes that have been raised at MOM level.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Currently, employers are required to notify MOM, if they intend to deploy their foreign domestic workers to an address that is different from what is stated in the work permit, particularly if they require the foreign domestic worker to take care of their charges such as young children or the elderly at a relative's home.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We are considering ways to enable the employer to be able to notify MOM more effectively so that we can track and approve such cases more consistently.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: She mentioned earlier that the review of the cases was such that there was a Caution and Advisory that was issued by MOM that was in line with other similar cases in the past.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Can Minister of State Gan clarify the reason for the additional review?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: MOM's actions against Mr Liew's family were based on the information available to our investigation officer during the period of the investigation from October 2017 to January 2018.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We all know arising from the High Court proceedings, there were observations made and there is a requirement for MOM to take into consideration the additional information provided to us, and hence, the review is on-going.
